subject: Dedicated commissioning cadence & acceptance playbook
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@helios.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:16:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated commissioning cadence & acceptance playbook

Sarah —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I pulled together a compact commissioning plan so Helios can move from Hosted API to a dedicated fleet with minimal risk and clear acceptance gates. Attached are: commissioning-checklist-v1.pdf (step-by-step cadence) and throughput-targets.csv (your expected token/sec & p50/p95 latency targets we discussed).

High level proposal (short):
- Pre-commissioning (week -2 to -1): config freeze, verification tokens & eval prompts, canary model build
- Commissioning (week 0): GPU allocation, image roll, smoke tests, KV cache priming, throughput runs (staging)
- Validation (week 1): across traffic profiles, fallback policies, rolling canary to 20% then 100%
- Cutover window (week 2): 2-hour blackout with rollback plan, post-cutover monitoring 72h

Acceptance gates (required to sign off):
1) Throughput within 10% of Hosted baseline for 95% of samples (see throughput-targets.csv)
2) End-to-end p95 latency <= 450ms for conversational flows under target batch sizing
3) No functional regressions on evaluation set (regression threshold: 1% failure)
4) Automated fallback to hosted model on capacity exceed / error spike

Can you confirm the proposed blackout windows (we suggested Tues 02:00–04:00 UTC) and if Helios wants H100-backed nodes or A100 for initial commissioning? H100 gives ~1.6x throughput on your LLM but we can stage on A100 if you prefer lower burn.

If that looks good I’ll loop in Ops and schedule a dry-run for next Tuesday.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: commissioning-checklist-v1.pdf (pdf, 420KB)
Attachment: throughput-targets.csv (csv, 8KB)

From: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@helios.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Platform Team <platform@helios.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commissioning cadence & acceptance playbook

Michael —

Appreciate the clear plan. Helios confirms the Tues 02:00–04:00 UTC blackout window works for us (that’s 18:00–20:00 PST). We prefer to commission on H100 nodes if Redwood can secure an initial pool for the first two weeks — we want to validate our peak prompt workloads. If there’s a cost delta we’ll accept it for the validation period.

Two questions before you loop Ops in:
- Can you call out the expected warmup token budget for KV priming we should budget during staging?
- For regression checks, we want a small validation slice that includes our identity redaction prompts + multi-turn context anchors — I’ll share that set by Monday.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lambert
Head of Platform
Helios AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commissioning cadence & acceptance playbook (internal)

Team —

Looping Ops into this once we confirm H100 pool. Quick notes from an engineering/validation perspective:
- Warmup budget: suggest 50M tokens to properly populate KV caches across the typical conversation prefixes Helios uses. That maps to ~2.5 hours of synthetic replay at 5k tokens/sec on an H100 80GB cluster.
- Throughput targets: I reviewed the throughput-targets.csv. For safety we should run three staged load tests: 1) smoke (10% load), 2) acceptance (50% target load sustained for 30m), 3) stress (125% burst for 5m).\n- Batching strategy: start with continuous batching + fixed batch window 10ms; if p95 exceeds threshold, move to adaptive batch windowing.
- Canary rollout: 1 node -> 10% traffic -> 20% -> 100% with 15m observation windows. Auto-fallback must be validated in staging with injected failures (OOM, GPU preemption).

Requested ops checklist items before dry-run:
- Reserve 4x H100 nodes in region us-west-2 for week 0 (tag: helios-DEAL-4832)
- Prepare canary AMI with quantized model image and KV cache warmers enabled
- Prepare throttling policy and fallback playbook (Doc: https://drive.redwood.com/helios/fallback-playbook)

Marissa — please confirm calendar availability for Tuesday dry-run and get me a short Ops runbook (bullet list) to attach to the customer. Olga — I’ll need your signoff on acceptance criteria wording (esp. the 1% regression threshold).

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commissioning cadence & acceptance playbook (approval)

Karthik / team —

I reviewed the acceptance gates and Karthik’s validation steps. I approve the proposed acceptance criteria with one small change: relax the latency p95 to 500ms during the first 24h post-cutover to allow for cache priming effects; after 24h it must meet <= 450ms. Update the commissioning-checklist-v1.pdf to reflect that temporal tolerance.

Operational approvals / immediate actions:
- Approve reservation: 4x H100 nodes (us-west-2) for week 0 — Ops to create reservation and attach tag helios-DEAL-4832.
- Dry-run schedule: Tues 02:00–04:00 UTC — Marissa please put a 90m dry-run on calendars (30m prep, 45m run, 15m retrospective).
- Attachments to customer: add a short rollback checklist and a DocuSign link for the Dedicated SLA amendment (I’ll provide the DocuSign link by EOD).

I’ll sign off on the final checklist once Karthik drops the Ops bullet runbook. Good work — keep the communication tight during the run.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: rollback-checklist.txt (txt, 1.2KB)
